<!-- Generated by Pixl from the skill "Write a merge request description", version 1. Edit it in the Skills tab, not here: changes made here are overwritten. -->

## Steps
1. Title: one line, imperative, at most 70 characters.
2. Why: one or two lines on the problem.
3. What changed: a short list by area, naming files.
4. How it was tested: the commands and their real results.
5. Risks and how to roll back.
6. Link the story.
7. Keep it under 30 lines.
## Checklist
- [ ] Title is imperative and short.
- [ ] Tested lists real commands and results.
- [ ] Risks are written, or "none known".
## Definition of done
A reviewer can decide to read the change from the description alone.
## Verify
Check every file you name was really changed. Check every test result is one you saw.
## Common mistakes
- A title like "updates".
- Listing what the code does line by line.
- Claiming tests you did not run.
- No rollback note for data or config changes.
## Example
Title: Give exactly 100 the 10% discount.
Why: orders of exactly 100 paid full price.
Changed: `shop.py` (`>` to `>=`), new `tests/test_edge.py`.
Tested: `python -m pytest -q`, 3 passed.
Risk: none known. Rollback: revert the commit.
